Keywords: nested stack, cloudformation reuse, stack composition
Guidance: A single monolithic template covering an entire environment becomes slow to update and hard to review; nested stacks split responsibility while sharing outputs via Fn::GetAtt.
Do: Break large templates into nested stacks per logical component (network, compute, data) linked via AWS::CloudFormation::Stack.
Don't: Maintain one multi-thousand-line template for an entire environment.
Example:
MyVPCStack:
  Type: AWS::CloudFormation::Stack
  Properties:
    TemplateURL: https://s3.../vpc.yaml

Keywords: change set, cloudformation preview, update stack
Guidance: Running UpdateStack directly applies changes immediately with no preview; a change set shows exactly what will be added, modified, or replaced before anything happens.
Do: Always create and review a change set before executing a stack update on production.
Don't: Call UpdateStack directly against production without previewing a change set.
Example: aws cloudformation create-change-set --stack-name prod --template-body file://template.yaml --change-set-name preview

Keywords: drift detection, manual console change, stack drift
Guidance: Manual console edits to CloudFormation-managed resources silently drift from the template; the next update can unexpectedly revert or conflict with that manual change.
Do: Run scheduled drift detection on production stacks and treat detected drift as an incident to reconcile, not ignore.
Don't: Allow manual console changes to CloudFormation-managed resources without ever running drift detection.

Topic: Stack policies to protect critical resources
Keywords: stack policy, resource protection, update protection
Guidance: Without a stack policy, an update targeting one resource can accidentally replace or delete an unrelated critical resource (like a production database) in the same stack.
Do: Attach a stack policy that denies Update/Replace/Delete on critical resources (e.g. databases) unless explicitly overridden.
Don't: Leave production stacks with no stack policy protecting stateful resources.

Guidance: Hardcoding one stack's resource IDs into another stack's parameters breaks the moment the source resource is recreated; Exports/Fn::ImportValue keeps them linked and validated.
Do: Use Outputs + Export in the producing stack and Fn::ImportValue in the consuming stack for cross-stack references.
Don't: Copy-paste a VPC ID as a hardcoded parameter value into a dependent stack's template.
Example:
Outputs:
  VpcId:
    Value: !Ref VPC
    Export:
      Name: shared-vpc-id

Keywords: rollback trigger, cloudwatch alarm, stack rollback
Guidance: Without rollback triggers tied to CloudWatch alarms, a deployment that passes CloudFormation's own checks but breaks the app in production won't automatically roll back.
Do: Configure RollbackConfiguration with CloudWatch alarms so a bad deploy auto-rolls-back on real application signals, not just resource-creation success.
Don't: Rely solely on CloudFormation's default success/failure signal with no application-level rollback trigger.

Guidance: Free-text CloudFormation parameters (e.g. environment name, instance type) with no AllowedValues/AllowedPattern let a typo create resources in the wrong shape silently.
Do: Constrain parameters with AllowedValues, AllowedPattern, or Min/MaxLength wherever the valid input set is known.
Don't: Leave a critical parameter like Environment as an unconstrained free-text String.
Example: Environment:\n  Type: String\n  AllowedValues: [dev, staging, prod]

Keywords: custom resource, lambda-backed resource, cloudformation extension
Guidance: Custom resources backed by a Lambda function that doesn't correctly signal SUCCESS/FAILED to the pre-signed S3 URL leave a stack stuck in *_IN_PROGRESS for the full timeout (often an hour).
Do: Always send a response (success or failure) from custom resource Lambda handlers, ideally using the cfn-response helper or Custom Resource Provider Framework.
Don't: Write a custom resource Lambda that can throw without ever sending a CloudFormation response.

Guidance: Manually deploying the same stack to dozens of accounts/regions via separate CLI calls doesn't scale and drifts as templates are updated in only some places.
Do: Use StackSets with a delegated administrator account to deploy and update a template consistently across accounts/regions.
Don't: Script individual per-account CloudFormation deploys for the same template across an AWS Organization.

Guidance: Deleting a stack by default deletes every resource in it, including databases and S3 buckets, unless DeletionPolicy explicitly says otherwise.
Do: Set DeletionPolicy: Retain (or Snapshot for RDS/EBS) on stateful resources so a stack deletion can't destroy data.
Don't: Leave the default Delete policy on production databases and data buckets.

Guidance: Syntax and best-practice errors caught only at deploy time waste a full create/update cycle; cfn-lint catches most of them locally or in CI in seconds.
Do: Run cfn-lint (and cfn_nag or similar for security checks) in CI before any deploy step.
Don't: Discover template errors only when CloudFormation rejects the deploy.

Guidance: CloudFormation refuses to create IAM resources without an explicit CAPABILITY acknowledgment, which exists specifically so IAM-creating deploys aren't accidental -- don't blanket-approve it in automation without review.
Do: Require CAPABILITY_IAM/CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM explicitly per deploy and review templates that create IAM resources before approving.
Don't: Add --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM to every pipeline by default without reviewing what IAM resources are being created.
Example: aws cloudformation deploy --template-file template.yaml --stack-name app --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM

Topic: Mappings vs Parameters for environment config
Guidance: Sprinkling !If conditions referencing raw parameter values throughout a template for per-environment sizing gets unreadable fast; a Mappings block centralizes that lookup.
Do: Use a Mappings block keyed by environment for per-environment values (instance size, AMI ID) instead of scattered Conditions.
Don't: Scatter Fn::If blocks referencing hardcoded environment strings throughout the template.

Guidance: Without a CreationPolicy/timeout, CloudFormation considers an EC2 instance 'created' as soon as it launches, even if the application bootstrap script inside it is still failing.
Do: Use CreationPolicy with cfn-signal so CloudFormation waits for the actual application to report ready, not just instance launch.
Don't: Assume instance launch success means the application bootstrap succeeded.
